cues: The law of dominance: in a hybrid only the dominant allele shows, while the recessive stays hidden but unchanged.
And the law of segregation, or purity of gametes: the two alleles separate when gametes form, so each gamete gets only one.
The physical reason is anaphase one of meiosis, when the two homologous chromosomes go to opposite poles.
text: Two laws follow. The law of dominance: in a hybrid only the dominant allele shows, while the recessive stays hidden but unchanged. And the law of segregation, or purity of gametes: the two alleles separate when gametes form, so each gamete gets only one. A gamete is never hybrid. The physical reason is anaphase one of meiosis, when the two homologous chromosomes go to opposite poles.
